summary: CrewSense is an integrated health monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration missions. Its core feature, the Daily Health Scan, brings all available health information into one dashboard: automatically retrieved sensor readings, manually entered measurements, imported laboratory results, and a short self-reported wellbeing check. Instead of judging each value against generic norms, CrewSense compares it with the astronaut’s personal baseline, highlights changes over time, raises alerts, and suggests next steps. This addresses the challenge by making gradual physiological change visible early, while the crew can still act, rather than leaving the data scattered across separate tools. Crews have limited time and limited medical support far from Earth, so one clear health overview supports both crew safety and mission success.
details:
CrewSense is a web application for daily astronaut health assessment. A Daily Health Scan opens with one dashboard that retrieves all available data from connected sources. The astronaut enters only the measurements that are missing, completes a short wellbeing assessment, and receives one consolidated health overview. The interface labels each data point by its origin: automatically retrieved sensor readings, manually entered measurements, imported laboratory or examination results, self-reported information, and missing or outdated data. The system never presents a measurement it cannot actually perform.

Analysis is personal. Each reading is compared with the astronaut’s own baseline, so the system shows changes over time rather than isolated values. It generates alerts, explains them in plain language, and lists recommended next steps.

The benefit is early visibility. Spaceflight health risks develop gradually, and a single value means little on its own. A consolidated, time-based view helps the crew and ground teams notice a trend before it becomes a problem.

Tools: frontend in React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, React Query, React Router, Dexie (IndexedDB for offline storage), Recharts (charts), and Vitest (tests). Backend in Python with FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, and Alembic migrations, using PostgreSQL 16 in production and SQLite for development. Deployment uses Vercel for the frontend and Fly.io for the backend.

Current status: the demo runs on seeded demo data. Connection to real sensors and laboratory systems is designed in the data model but not yet implemented.

Creativity: the system treats the astronaut’s personal baseline as the reference point, and it presents every value with its source, so the crew can judge the data’s reliability.
